issue_context.title: net.Listen listens on all available unicast and anycast IP addresses regarding the IP family
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

There are flag descriptions where is stated that the unspecified address behaves differently depending on the IP family:

```
(set to 0.0.0.0 for all IPv4 interfaces and :: for all IPv6 interfaces)
```

However, that's not the behavior implemented in `net.Listen`  and `net.ListenPacket`, clarified in the golang documentation https://github.com/golang/go/commit/424b0654f8e6c72f69e096f69009096de16e30fa

> // For TCP networks, if the host in the address parameter is empty or
> // a literal unspecified IP address, Listen listens on all available
> // unicast and anycast IP addresses of the local system.
> // To only use IPv4, use network "tcp4".

**What you expected to happen**:

Fix the comment to state the reality,  i.e
```
 (set 0.0.0.0 or :: for all interfaces")
```

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

From the root of the kubernetes repo
```sh
grep -r "for all IPv4 interfaces"
...
cmd/kubelet/app/options/options.go:     fs.Var(utilflag.IPVar{Val: &c.HealthzBindAddress}, "healthz-bind-address", "The IP address for the healthz server to serve on (set to `0.0.0.0` for all IPv4 interfaces and `::` for all IPv6 interfaces)")
cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go:   fs.Var(utilflag.IPVar{Val: &o.config.BindAddress}, "bind-address", "The IP address for the proxy server to serve on (set to `0.0.0.0` for all IPv4 interfaces and `::` for all IPv6 interfaces)")
cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go:   fs.Var(utilflag.IPVar{Val: &o.config.HealthzBindAddress}, "healthz-bind-address", "The IP address for the health check server to serve on (set to `0.0.0.0` for all IPv4 interfaces and `::` for all IPv6 interfaces)")
```

I am very much in favor of this.  Being correct and precise in these flags is valuable.

To convince myself you were right, I wrote this program:

```
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
)

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) != 2 {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "usage: %s <listen_addr>\n", os.Args[0])
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	addr := os.Args[1]
	_, err := net.Listen("tcp", net.JoinHostPort(addr, "12345"))
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "ERROR: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	cmd := exec.Command("bash", "-c", "netstat -nap 2>&1 | grep :12345")
	b, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "ERROR: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(3)
	}
	fmt.Println(string(b))
}
```

And then I ran it for various inputs:

```
thockin@thockin-glaptop3:/tmp$ go run net.go ""
tcp6       0      0 :::12345                :::*                    LISTEN      256251/net          

thockin@thockin-glaptop3:/tmp$ go run net.go "::"
tcp6       0      0 :::12345                :::*                    LISTEN      256343/net          

thockin@thockin-glaptop3:/tmp$ go run net.go "0.0.0.0"
tcp6       0      0 :::12345                :::*                    LISTEN      256431/net          

thockin@thockin-glaptop3:/tmp$ go run net.go "$(hostname -i)"
tcp        0      0 127.0.1.1:12345         0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      256529/net          

thockin@thockin-glaptop3:/tmp$ go run net.go "localhost"
tcp        0      0 127.0.0.1:12345         0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      256613/net          
```

In these flags and docs, we should be clear that if you are specifying a v6 addr and port you have to use `[ip]:port` syntax.

Or maybe we should just audit and fix ALL such places to support and document that "nothing" is how you specify all interfaces.  E.g. --bind-address=":80" is more obvious than either "0.0.0.0:80" or "[::]:80".  Even if those syntaxes work, let's just make "" the norm?
